Relevance: Adam’s divinely taught knowledge establishes an epistemic dimension of human distinction; it is not an inventory of particular sciences.

Relevance: Linguistic and physical diversity is presented among divine signs. Cultural unity therefore need not mean one language or ethnicity.

Translations / status: Sahih International (English); Fateh Muhammad Jalandhari (Urdu). Arabic and both excerpts checked at the links below.
Relevance: The verse names homes, portable shelters and furnishings. These are direct examples of material life, not a complete theory of civilization.

en.text: Source: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 71; Knowledge, Book 3; chapter 13.
Published English excerpt: If Allah wants to do good to a person, He makes him comprehend the religion.
Grade: Sahih; included in the named Sahih collection.
Text sources: Arabic / English / numbering: Sunnah.com. Urdu: Islamic Urdu Books; wording checked, individual translator not independently established.
Parallel: Sahih Muslim, no. 1037a; wording may vary. Same counted entry.
Relevance: Understanding, rather than mere repetition, is praised. This passage directly concerns religious understanding, not every technical discipline.

Locator: Hud 11:61; discussion of wa-stamarakum fiha.

Scholarly position / paraphrased argument: Al-Qurtubi records habitation and cultivation/building interpretations, then discusses whether the expression implies obligation through linguistic and juristic reasoning.
Access / status: Arabic commentary inspected in SurahQuran’s digital reproduction; compiler’s paraphrase. URL page numbers are not a verified printed-edition pagination.
Relevance: A civilizational duty should not be asserted merely by substituting a modern slogan for this debated expression.

علمی مؤقف / مفہومی خلاصہ: قرطبی رہائش اور کھیتی و تعمیر کے مفاہیم نقل کرتے ہیں؛ پھر لغوی و فقہی استدلال سے بحث کرتے ہیں کہ عبارت وجوب پر دلالت کرتی ہے یا نہیں۔
رسائی / حیثیت: سورہ قرآن کی رقمی نقل میں عربی تفسیر دیکھی گئی؛ مرتب کا مفہومی خلاصہ ہے۔ ویب پتے کے صفحہ نمبر کو کسی مطبوعہ نسخے کی تحقیق شدہ جلد و صفحہ نہ سمجھیں۔
مطابقت: اس زیرِ بحث تعبیر کی جگہ جدید نعرہ رکھ کر تمدنی فرض کا دعویٰ نہ کیا جائے۔

en.text: Locator: Chapter I, first prefatory discussion: human social organization.
Scholarly position / paraphrased argument: Ibn Khaldun argues that food, tools and protection require cooperation: an isolated individual cannot ordinarily supply the combined labour needed for life.
Access / status: Franz Rosenthal’s English translation inspected in the MuslimPhilosophy digital reproduction; compiler’s paraphrase. Printed edition and pagination not verified.
Relevance: A conceptual foundation for civilization as organized interdependence, not architecture alone.

ur.text: ماخذ: ابن خلدون؛ المقدمہ۔
محل: باب اول، پہلا تمہیدی مقدمہ: انسانی اجتماع۔
علمی مؤقف / مفہومی خلاصہ: ابن خلدون کے مطابق خوراک، آلات اور حفاظت تعاون چاہتے ہیں؛ تنہا فرد عموماً زندگی کے لیے درکار مجموعی محنت فراہم نہیں کر سکتا۔
رسائی / حیثیت: مسلم فلاسفی کی رقمی نقل میں فرانز روزنتھال کا انگریزی ترجمہ دیکھا گیا؛ مرتب کا مفہومی خلاصہ ہے۔ مطبوعہ نسخہ اور صفحہ بندی کی تحقیق نہیں کی گئی۔
مطابقت: تہذیب کو صرف عمارتوں کے بجائے منظم باہمی انحصار سمجھنے کی بنیاد ہے۔

entries.subtitleEn: Umran and necessary cooperation

en.text: Locator: Chapter V, section 30, craft of book production; textual correction and transmission.

Scholarly position / paraphrased argument: Copying, correction and binding form an urban craft. Reliable transmission is emphasized so that statements and legal opinions are not falsely attributed to authors.
Exact English excerpt (Rosenthal): These were copied, bound, and corrected with the help of a transmission technique
Access / status: Franz Rosenthal’s English translation inspected in the MuslimPhilosophy digital reproduction; compiler’s paraphrase. Printed edition and pagination not verified.
Relevance: Shows how material book culture and scholarly reliability interact; the author’s regional decline judgments remain historical claims.

ur.text: ماخذ: ابن خلدون؛ المقدمہ۔

en.text: Locator: Chapter VI, section 37, auxiliary sciences.

Scholarly position / paraphrased argument: He distinguishes disciplines studied as ends from instrumental disciplines and warns that excessive preliminary detail can prevent students from reaching their main subjects.
Access / status: Franz Rosenthal’s English translation inspected in the MuslimPhilosophy digital reproduction; compiler’s paraphrase. Printed edition and pagination not verified.
Relevance: An educational priority argument, not a blanket rejection of grammar, arithmetic or logic.

en.text: Source: Abu Hamid al-Ghazali; Ihya Ulum al-Din, Book I: The Book of Knowledge.
Locator: Section II, personally obligatory knowledge.
Scholarly position / paraphrased argument: Personally required knowledge expands with actual duties and circumstances, such as worship, trading and avoiding relevant moral faults.
Access / status: Nabih Amin Faris’s English translation, Sh. Muhammad Ashraf, Lahore, digitized at Ghazali.org, inspected; compiler’s paraphrase. Edition/year and print pages not verified.
Relevance: Use for connecting education to lived responsibility.

ur.text: ماخذ: ابو حامد الغزالی؛ احیاء علوم الدین، کتاب العلم۔
محل: حصہ دوم، فرضِ عین علم۔
علمی مؤقف / مفہومی خلاصہ: شخصی واجب علم عملی ذمہ داریوں اور حالات کے مطابق بڑھتا ہے، جیسے عبادات، تجارت اور متعلقہ اخلاقی خرابیوں سے بچاؤ۔
رسائی / حیثیت: نبیہ امین فارس کا انگریزی ترجمہ، شیخ محمد اشرف، لاہور؛ غزالی ڈاٹ آرگ پر متن دیکھا گیا۔ مرتب کا مفہومی خلاصہ ہے؛ نسخہ، سال اور مطبوعہ صفحات کی تحقیق نہیں کی گئی۔
مطابقت: تعلیم اور عملی ذمہ داری کا ربط واضح کرنے میں مفید ہے۔

en.text: Source: UNESCO; UNESCO Universal Declaration on Cultural Diversity, adopted 2 November 2001.
Locator: Preamble, definition of culture; Article 3.

Scholarly position / paraphrased argument: Culture includes spiritual, material, intellectual and emotional features, ways of living, values and beliefs; development is not reduced to economic growth.
Access / status: Official declaration text inspected; compiler’s paraphrase. Modern comparative institutional source, not a source of Islamic revelation or fiqh.
Relevance: A comparative vocabulary, not a claim that modern and Islamic frameworks are identical.

ur.text: ماخذ: یونیسکو؛ ثقافتی تنوع کا عالمی اعلامیہ، منظور شدہ 2 نومبر 2001۔
محل: تمہید، ثقافت کی تعریف؛ دفعہ 3۔
علمی مؤقف / مفہومی خلاصہ: ثقافت میں روحانی، مادی، علمی و جذباتی خصوصیات، طرزِ زندگی، اقدار اور عقائد شامل ہیں؛ ترقی محض معاشی نمو نہیں۔
رسائی / حیثیت: اعلامیے کا سرکاری متن دیکھا گیا؛ مرتب کا مفہومی خلاصہ ہے۔ جدید تقابلی ادارہ جاتی ماخذ ہے، اسلامی وحی یا فقہ کا اصل ماخذ نہیں۔
مطابقت: تقابلی اصطلاحات کا ماخذ ہے، جدید اور اسلامی تصورات کی یکسانیت کا دعویٰ نہیں۔

en.text: Source: Department of Islamic Art, The Metropolitan Museum of Art; Calligraphy in Islamic Art, Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History; New York: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, October 2001.
Locator: Main essay, discussion of script, function and regional variation.
Scholarly position / paraphrased argument: Calligraphy carries textual meaning while functioning decoratively; scripts and uses vary across regions, periods and objects.
Access / status: Official curatorial essay inspected; secondary historical analysis, not direct inspection of every underlying manuscript or object. Compiler’s paraphrase.
Relevance: Demonstrates a vital cultural element without claiming that every historical artistic choice is religiously prescribed.

en.text: Source: Department of Islamic Art, The Metropolitan Museum of Art; Geometric Patterns in Islamic Art, Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History; New York: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, October 2001.
Locator: Main essay, origins and development of geometric ornament.

Scholarly position / paraphrased argument: Earlier Greek, Roman and Sasanian motifs were transformed into complex decorative systems, illustrating adaptation rather than cultural development in isolation.
Access / status: Official curatorial essay inspected; secondary historical analysis, not direct inspection of every underlying manuscript or object. Compiler’s paraphrase.
Relevance: Do not infer that all Islamic art is geometric or non-figural.

en.text: Source: Department of Islamic Art, The Metropolitan Museum of Art; The Nature of Islamic Art, Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History; New York: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, October 2001.
Locator: Opening definition and discussion of regional styles.

Scholarly position / paraphrased argument: The category includes religious works and wider art produced in Muslim-ruled lands, for Muslim patrons or by Muslim artists; it is not confined to mosque objects.
Access / status: Official curatorial essay inspected; secondary historical analysis, not direct inspection of every underlying manuscript or object. Compiler’s paraphrase.
Relevance: Distinguishes a historical-cultural classification from a judgment that each object expresses an Islamic legal ideal.
